sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
நாற்கவியும் போற்றும் நாரணன் மனோகரியே
பாற்கடல் துயில் கொள்ளும் பரந்தாமன் பத்தினியே
sections.translit:
nARkaviyum pOtRum nAraNan manOgariyE
pArkadal thuyil koLLum parandhAman patthiniyE
sections.en: Four types of Tamil poetry glorify Lord Narayana’s wife, Goddess Lakshmi. She is the consort of the Lord who sleeps in the milky ocean.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
கார்முகில் வண்ணன் மார்பிடை அமர்ந்தாய்
பார்மிசை அடியார் நெஞ்செல்லாம் நிறைந்தாய்
sections.translit:
kArmugil vaNNan mArbidai amarndhAy
pArmisai adiyAr nenjellAm niRaindhAy
sections.en: Devi, you are seated in the chest of the god who matches the hue of dark clouds. You are domiciled in the hearts of your devotees.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
கையில் கபாலம் ஏந்தி அலைந்த அரனும்
தையல் உன்னால் விமோசனம் அடைந்தாரன்றோ
வையம் உய்யவே வளமெலாம் பெருகிடவே
பையவே வருவாய் பசுமை உருவே நற்திருவே
sections.translit:
kaiyil kapAlam Endhi alaindha aranum
thaiyal unnAl vimOchanam adaindhArandRO
vaiyam uyyavE vaLamelAm perugidavE
paiyavE varuvAy pasumai uruvE naRthiruvE
sections.en: Is it not true that Siva wandered the earth with the skull of Brahma in his hand, and that you finally released him from this curse? Your grace is responsible for fertile farms and inestimable treasures. Please come with your gentle steps and offer peace and abundant prosperity to this world.

notes: In the Tamil language, songs are classified based on four classic Tamil Meters. Most of the poetry thus fall into four “Pa” super class of poetry. Basically “Pa” represents Osai or harmonics. The four subtypes are called VeN, Aasiriyam, Kali and Vanji. The classification is laid out in the ancient Tamil Grammar text, Tholkappiyam. This is what is referenced in the Pallavi. Four Subtypes of Tamil “Pa” The charanam refers to Lord Siva’s plight after his wrathful act with the Lord of creation. Siva inherited Brahmahathi dosham because he plucked the fifth head of Lord Brahma. He developed an insatiable hunger. The skull of Brahma got stuck in his arms and Siva was wandering the earth begging for food. The skull – which he was using as a bowl – would not fill up until he reached the Bikshandar Koil and begged for alms from Poornavalli Thayar (Goddess Lakshmi). Once Lakshmi offered him alms, the bowl was full and his hunger was relieved. Uthamar Temple Sthalapuranam Siva went to Thirukandiyur and prayed to Lord Vishnu and got the kapalam or skull removed from his arm, and thus was completely absolved of his sins. Here, Vishnu is known as Hara Saaba Vimochanar in Thirukandiyur.
